micropubr

Publication-ready microbiome visualizations with one line of code.

micropubr is a unified, opinionated R package for turning a phyloseq object into a journal-quality figure with a single call. It applies one consistent design philosophy across the whole microbiome workflow — shared argument names, colourblind-safe defaults, automatic statistical overlays and reproducible, auto-generated captions — so that every analysis, from alpha diversity to machine learning, is produced the same way.

Every mp_*() plotting function returns a plain ggplot2 object, so you keep full control: just add + theme(...) or any other layer. Pass interactive = TRUE to get a plotly widget instead — same call, hover tooltips and zoom included.

Why micropubr?

Most microbiome figures today are hand-assembled from phyloseq, vegan, ggplot2, ggtree and a dozen helpers — dozens of lines per panel, redone for every paper. micropubr collapses each of these into one consistent call:

Task base phyloseq + ggplot2 micropubr
Ordination with PERMANOVA + ellipses ~25 lines mp_ordination(ps, group.by = "Group")
Alpha diversity with significance brackets ~20 lines mp_alpha(ps, group.by = "Group")
Top-N stacked composition ~15 lines mp_taxa(ps, tax.level = "Genus")

Features

  • One consistent interface. A single family of mp_*() functions with shared argument names (group.by, palette, theme, plot.title, return.data, …) spanning diversity, composition, differential abundance, phylogenetics, networks, longitudinal data, functional profiles, machine learning and genomics.
  • Publication defaults out of the box. Colourblind-safe palettes, a clean journal theme, sensible typography and automatic, reproducible figure captions on every plot.
  • Statistics built in. Kruskal–Wallis / pairwise tests, PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, ANOSIM, MRPP, Mantel tests, variation partitioning and indicator species analysis are computed and annotated automatically.
  • Static or interactive. Every ggplot-based function accepts interactive = TRUE to return a linked plotly widget with the same call.
  • Composable and exportable. Combine panels with mp_combine() and write figures at journal column widths (or as self-contained HTML) with mp_export().
  • ggplot2 all the way down. Plots are ordinary ggplot objects — extend them with any layer, theme or scale you like.
  • return.data = TRUE everywhere. Every function can hand back the tidy data frame (and, where relevant, the fitted model) behind the figure.
  • Differential abundance done carefully. mp_run_da() runs Wilcoxon, covariate-adjusted linear (mixed) models, ANCOM-BC2, DESeq2 and ALDEx2 on one shared design, for two or many groups, and mp_diff() shows where they agree.
  • Figures that write their own methods. Every figure records what was computed; mp_methods() turns that into a methods paragraph with versions and references, and mp_alt_text() into accessible alt text.
  • Statistical guardrails. Small groups, richness compared across very uneven depths, and a PERMANOVA undermined by unequal dispersions are flagged as they happen.
  • phyloseq or TreeSummarizedExperiment. Every function accepts either container, so the mia / OMA ecosystem works out of the box.

Installation 

# Core dependencies (Bioconductor + CRAN)
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("phyloseq")

# micropubr (development version)
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("daniilidisK/micropubr")

Optional features pull in additional packages on demand: plotly / htmlwidgets (interactive plots), ggtree / ggtreeExtra (trees), ggraph / igraph (networks), ggalluvial (longitudinal), treemapify (treemaps), circlize (chord / Circos figures), randomForest / xgboost / pROC (machine learning), DESeq2 / ALDEx2 / ANCOMBC (differential abundance), SpiecEasi (network inference), Rsamtools / GenomicAlignments (coverage), ShortRead (FASTQ quality), qiime2R / biomformat (import) and shiny (interactive explorer).

Quick start 

library(micropubr)
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")

# Alpha diversity with automatic Kruskal–Wallis + pairwise brackets
mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),
         group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal")

# Beta diversity: PCoA on Bray–Curtis with ellipses + PERMANOVA caption
mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",
              group.by = "SampleType")

# Taxonomic composition: top 10 phyla, faceted by sample type
mp_taxa(GlobalPatterns, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType")

# Compose a multi-panel figure and export at journal column width
fig <- mp_combine(
  mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType"),
  mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType"),
  ncol = 2, tag.levels = "A"
)
mp_export(fig, "figure1.pdf", column = "double", dpi = 600)

Interactive figures

Add interactive = TRUE to any plotting function to get a live plotly widget — hover for tooltips, zoom and pan, and toggle groups via the legend. Multiple panels are linked into a single plotly::subplot(), and mp_export() saves the result to a self-contained HTML page.

# An interactive ordination
mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)

# Save any interactive figure to a shareable web page
w <- mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)
mp_export(w, "alpha.html")

The circular circlize-based figures (mp_chord(), mp_circos(), mp_coverage()) are not ggplot2 objects, so they have no interactive mode.

Function reference

Core visualizations

Function Purpose
mp_alpha() Alpha diversity (box / violin / dot / rarefaction) with tests
mp_ordination() PCoA / NMDS / PCA / RDA / CCA / dbRDA with PERMANOVA
mp_taxa() Composition: bar / area / heatmap / bubble / treemap
mp_diff() Differential abundance: volcano / MA / forest / dot / heatmap / consensus / structural zeros / concordance
mp_tree() Annotated phylogenetic trees (abundance + taxonomy rings)
mp_network() Co-occurrence / correlation networks
mp_longitudinal() Spaghetti / trajectory / alluvial / horizon over time
mp_function() Functional pathway profiles (PICRUSt2 / HUMAnN)

Statistics and ecology

Function Purpose
mp_dispersion() Multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP) with ANOSIM / MRPP / PERMANOVA
mp_mantel() Mantel test between community and explanatory distances
mp_varpart() Variation partitioning across explanatory matrices
mp_prevalence() Prevalence–abundance and core-microbiome plots
mp_indicator() Indicator species analysis
mp_ml() Machine learning (random forest / xgboost): importance, ROC, confusion
mp_run_da() Run one or several differential-abundance methods (with covariates, repeated measures and multi-group contrasts) and return one tidy table

Genomics and quality control

Function Purpose
mp_coverage() Genome / contig sequencing-depth (coverage) tracks from BAM/CRAM
mp_circos() Circular (Circos-style) genome plot with coverage / GC / link tracks
mp_chord() Chord diagram linking top taxa to a grouping variable
mp_qc_profile() Per-cycle FASTQ read-quality profiles (DADA2 truncation)

Reporting

Function Purpose
mp_methods() Methods paragraph, software versions, references and statistical notes for a set of figures
mp_alt_text() Accessible alt text describing a figure and its key result

Infrastructure

Function Purpose
mp_combine() Compose multi-panel figures with shared legends and tags
mp_export() Save static figures (PDF/PNG/…) or interactive widgets (HTML)
mp_palette(), mp_palettes() Colourblind-safe qualitative / sequential / diverging palettes
mp_theme_publication(), mp_theme_nature(), mp_theme_cell(), mp_theme_dark() Journal-style themes
mp_darken() Recolour a finished figure for a dark background, keeping its layout
mp_set_defaults(), mp_get_defaults(), mp_reset_defaults() Package-wide defaults
mp_import_qiime2(), mp_import_dada2(), mp_import_biom(), mp_import_metaphlan() Import to phyloseq
mp_as_phyloseq() Convert a TreeSummarizedExperiment (accepted directly by every function)
mp_explore() Interactive Shiny explorer that emits reproducible code

Differential abundance with several methods

Differential-abundance methods are known to disagree, and unadjusted tests are easily confounded. mp_run_da() therefore runs one or several methods on a single shared design and returns one long table (feature, contrast, method, log2FC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, robust, structural_zero):

method Model Covariates (adjust) Repeated measures (random)
"wilcox" Wilcoxon rank-sum on CLR values (default, no extra packages) – –
"lm" Linear model on CLR values; mixed model with random ✓ ✓ (lmerTest)
"ancombc2" ANCOM-BC2: bias correction, structural zeros, pseudo-count sensitivity ✓ ✓
"deseq2" DESeq2 Wald test, poscounts size factors ✓ –
"aldex2" ALDEx2 Welch’s t-test on Monte-Carlo CLR instances – – 
gp <- phyloseq::subset_samples(GlobalPatterns,
                               SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Skin", "Tongue"))

# All groups against a reference, three methods on one design
da <- mp_run_da(gp, group.by = "SampleType", reference = "Skin",
                method = c("wilcox", "lm", "ancombc2"), tax.level = "Genus")

# With your own metadata: adjust for confounders, model repeated measures
# mp_run_da(ps, group.by = "Treatment", method = c("lm", "ancombc2"),
#           adjust = c("Age", "Sex"), random = "Subject")

mp_diff(da, plot.type = "consensus")   # which methods agree, taxon by taxon
mp_diff(da, plot.type = "heatmap")     # fold changes across contrasts
mp_diff(da, plot.type = "volcano", contrast = "Feces vs Skin")
mp_diff(da, plot.type = "zeros")       # ANCOM-BC2 structural zeros

Fold changes are always log2 (ANCOM-BC2’s natural-log estimates are converted), and ANCOM-BC2 results that fail its pseudo-count sensitivity analysis are not counted as significant unless you pass robust.only = FALSE. mp_diff() also reads results produced elsewhere — DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC/ANCOM-BC2 objects, any data frame, or a named list of them for a consensus or concordance plot:

mp_diff(list(DESeq2 = deseq_res, ALDEx2 = aldex_res), plot.type = "consensus")

Methods text, alt text and statistical guardrails

Every figure records the analysis behind it: the tests and their settings, transformations, filters, multiple-testing correction, group sizes and package versions. mp_methods() turns those records into a methods paragraph with references, ready to edit into a manuscript; mp_alt_text() writes alt text for the figure.

p1 <- mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal")
p2 <- mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType")
mp_methods(p1, p2)                   # or mp_methods() for every figure so far
mp_methods(p1, p2, format = "markdown")
mp_alt_text(p2)

While figures are made, micropubr also checks for conditions under which their statistics are easy to over-read — groups smaller than five samples, richness compared across a more than ten-fold range of sequencing depth, a significant PERMANOVA alongside unequal dispersions (PERMDISP), a method that had to ignore the covariates you asked for, a covariate so entangled with the grouping that adjusting for it is unstable — and warns. The same notes are listed by mp_methods(); mp_set_defaults(guardrails = "caption") writes them into the figure caption instead, and "off" silences them.

Palettes and theming

All palettes are colourblind-tolerant and designed for microbiome figures — qualitative palettes for taxa and groups, plus sequential and diverging ramps for heatmaps and continuous overlays.

mp_palettes()               # list available palettes
mp_palette("taxa10")        # a qualitative palette
mp_palette("diverging", n = 7)

# Swap the theme on any figure
mp_taxa(GlobalPatterns, tax.level = "Phylum", theme = mp_theme_nature())

Package-wide defaults

Set a house style once and every mp_*() function will pick it up:

mp_set_defaults(font.size = 9, palette = "okabe")
mp_get_defaults()
mp_reset_defaults()

Importing data

Bring data in from the common upstream pipelines and get a phyloseq object back, ready for the rest of the family:

ps <- mp_import_qiime2(
  features = "table.qza",
  taxonomy = "taxonomy.qza",
  metadata = "metadata.tsv"
)

Importers are also provided for DADA2 (mp_import_dada2()), BIOM (mp_import_biom()) and MetaPhlAn (mp_import_metaphlan()).

Data already in Bioconductor’s TreeSummarizedExperiment (for example from mia) needs no conversion: every mp_*() function accepts it directly, and mp_as_phyloseq() converts it explicitly when you want the phyloseq object.
